ecologyTesoro:
Tesoro Refinery

We regulate water, hazardous waste, and cleanup activities at the Tesoro Refining & Marketing Company in Anacortes.

Facility information

The refinery began operating in 1955. Owned by Marathon and doing business as Tesoro, it processes crude oil into a variety of petroleum products and has about 330 employees and 280 contractors that work on the site.

  • At full production, the refinery has the ability to process 120,000 barrels of crude oil each day.
  • Wastewater from the petroleum-making process is treated and sent to Fidalgo Bay.

Permit information

  • Wastewater permit
    • Support document
  • Hazardous wast corrective action permit 
    • Support document

The Northwest Clean Air Agency regulates the refinery’s air quality activities. Visit the Northwest Clean Air Agency website or call 800-622-4627 for more information.

Tesoro contacts

Company website
Facility phone: 360-428-1617 or 800-622-4627
Location: West March Point Road, Anacortes, Wash.

The Department of Ecology issed a notice of penalty to Tesoro Refinery in Anacortes (Skagit County) for $1,397,000 for Dangerous Waste violations that took place for nine months between 2024 and 2025.

  • Penalty Document

Read our news release.

What happened?

Tesoro’s penalty is related to its handling of the Marathon Anacortes Refinery’s neutralization pond, a 150,000-gallon artificial basin that held spent sulfuric acid from its industrial process. The wastewater was frequently about the same pH as battery acid, qualifying it as a dangerous waste (pH of 2 or less at any given time). The acidity in the pond needed to be controlled to prevent potential damage to the pond’s liner and a potential toxic release. Inspectors flagged the problem in 2022 and later began requiring regular testing of the pond, which revealed that dangerous acidity was an ongoing problem. It took Tesoro nine months to implement an alternative management method for the waste, increasing the risks for a potential release from the pond. Tesoro is working with Ecology to remove the remaining residue in the pond..

The company may appeal Ecology’s decision with 30 days to the Washington Pollution Control Hearings Board.
